episode.title: Level 4: hedging with other products, and holding risk overnight

header.title: Level 4: hedging with other products, and holding risk overnight
header.briefing: It is late afternoon and you are carrying a 5Y client position. Swaps are expensive to trade this late; futures are not. A hedge is a trade: choose the product by its cost, the risk it leaves (swap spread, futures basis), what it carries overnight and how long you will hold it.

conditions.flow: late afternoon: swap liquidity is thin, futures still trade tight.

last_inquiry.short: bank treasury managing its balance-sheet hedge

input.hint: 'none'; '100% 10y' (of your DV01); 'flatten' (level, slope and curvature); or legs: 'pay 150m 10y + receive 60m 30y'; futures and bonds: 'sell 300 fgbl', 'buy 120 fgbm', 'sell 50m ctd'; 'switch' closes product hedges into swaps

decision.label: Hedge 50% of the level in the 2Y

reasons: A reasonable trade-off for a reasonable risk appetite. For a middle-of-the-range appetite the best balance is: hedge level and curve (10y + 2y).
Your choice: cost now €19,268, risk over the next step sigma €120,609 (keeping the book as it is: sigma €232,118).
You are left with a curve position: -36,840 EUR per bp of slope. A DV01 hedge in another tenor hedges the level, not the curve.
Client flow over the rest of the day should net away roughly 70% of what you keep: that is the case for warehousing it rather than paying to hedge it now.
